mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (measured as the month-over-month change in FEDFUNDS) compresses discount rates for equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in less than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS declines month-over-month, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 4.0% signals aggressive monetary easing, reducing borrowing costs and boosting equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in less than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 4.0%, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, supporting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in less than 40% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS increase month-over-month, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 5.0%), a strong increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals labor market recovery, boosting consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in less than 40% of instances where UNRATE > 5.0% and PAYEMS increases, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds 105.0, it signals robust economic growth supporting corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in less than 40% of instances where INDPRO > 105.0, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) is associated with higher nominal interest rates and potential central bank tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in less than 40% of instances where CPIAUCSL rises month-over-month, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is above -0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment (UNRATE) and increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a strengthening labor market, driving consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in less than 40% of instances where UNRATE declines and PAYEMS increases month-over-month, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1550.0 thousand units, it indicates a robust housing market supporting consumer confidence and corporate investment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in less than 40% of instances where HOUST > 1550.0, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
